title: Creating Meshes (Blender 2.80 Fundamentals)
goal: Learn the difference between adding a mesh in Object Mode (a new object) and in Edit Mode (more geometry inside the current object).

source.kind: hand-written answer key, to grade the steps Muse Spark extracts from the video
source.author: Blender Studio
source.note: The video uses Blender 2.80; the steps are written for the default scene of Blender 5.2 and keep going in one scene where the video restarts from a fresh file.

steps.instruction: In Object Mode, add a UV sphere (Add > Mesh > UV Sphere). It becomes a new object.
Move the sphere away from the cube with G so they no longer overlap.
Add a monkey (Add > Mesh > Monkey), another new object.
Move the monkey away from the cube with G.
Select the cube and switch to Edit Mode (Tab).
Still in Edit Mode, add a UV sphere: it becomes part of the cube's mesh, not a new object.
Move the new sphere geometry out of the cube with G.
Go back to Object Mode (Tab): the cube object now contains both shapes.
